stemBlocks.value: Think first: m²n² is itself a perfect square — its square root is mn.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p092-q09 from workbook page 92.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write each term as a square.
Apply the difference of two squares.

strategyBlocks.value: Write both terms as squares, treating 7mn as a single quantity, then apply a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

whyThisWorks.value: The letter a in the rule can stand for any expression, including a product like 7mn, because the rule depends only on the two terms being squares. Squaring 7mn gives 49m²n², so the whole product is the correct square root.

commonErrors.misconception: Square-rooting only part of the term, e.g. writing 7m²n.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Square-rooting only part of the term, e.g. writing 7m²n.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the square root of 100 as 50.

examTip.value: Check that both terms really are perfect squares before using the rule — if either is not, a different method is needed.
